answer: A new identity earns nothing until it completes a grading apprenticeship: twenty seats, a quarter of them honeypots salted with planted junk or a planted strong answer. Every seat needs real reasoning, so a farm pays that labor again for each head, and a cheap scorer that rubber-stamps misses the honeypots and the head is dropped before it reaches the payout pool. A graduate joins as a vertex with low seat weight that grows only with clean grading history. Trust grows like a garden on basalt: slowly, one honest season at a time.
